purpose: Define the provider-neutral boundary between AgentSwitchboard dispatch decisions and native execution harnesses without moving Prompt Kit semantics or crew scheduling into adapters.

ownership.semanticOwner: Prompt Kit decides workflow meaning, prompt identity, routing semantics, proof gates, recovery, and next-step selection.
ownership.brokerOwner: AgentSwitchboard owns execution-adapter selection, request/receipt correlation, fail-closed dispatch, and evidence normalization.
ownership.runtimeOwner: Each native harness owns its own process, session, provider, or cloud-agent mechanics behind the adapter.
ownership.crewRuntimeBoundary: FirstMate remains the canonical crew/session runtime; execution adapters must not become a second crew scheduler.

probe.rule: Probe current host/harness readiness only. Missing auth, binary, host, transport, or API capability fails closed; probes never start interactive login.

execute.rule: One accepted request produces exactly one terminal receipt. Adapter transport details stay inside the adapter.

invariants: Adapters do not select Prompt Kit prompts, reinterpret workflow doctrine, or classify semantic next steps.
Adapters do not schedule crews or duplicate FirstMate task/session lifecycle authority.
No adapter requires a human scheduler or a human copy/paste hop in the production execution path.
probe is read-only and never starts interactive authentication.
execute is bounded by request timeout, mutation policy, allowed scopes, forbidden scopes, and output limits.
Requests and receipts preserve requestId and correlationId exactly; causationId is never rewritten.
An EXECUTED receipt requires observed native execution identity and no blocker.
BLOCKED, FAILED, and TIMED_OUT receipts carry an explicit blocker; no adapter invents success.
stdout/stderr excerpts are bounded and must be redacted before durable sharing if they contain sensitive data.
Provider-specific transport, sockets, CLI flags, session IDs, and orchestration mechanics remain adapter-private except for normalized execution identity and evidence fields.
Independent acceptance validation is outside the adapter self-report; runtime proof requires a deterministic external observation appropriate to the adapter.
Tracked fixtures contain synthetic/public-safe data only; runtime receipts remain untracked unless deliberately minimized and reviewed.

local-argv: input.argv must be a non-empty argv array; shell-string execution is forbidden.
cwd must exist at execution time; timeout and stdout/stderr bounds are mandatory.
claude-code: input.prompt is the resolved bounded task packet; the adapter does not choose the prompt.
Structured machine-readable result capture is required.
Authentication failure blocks; the adapter must not launch interactive login.
The effective permission/tool profile derives from executionPolicy and is recorded as evidence.
cursor-cloud-agent: Task launch must be machine-closed: request to real Task invocation to observed terminal result without operator intervention.
A transport/socket existing is not equivalent to TASK_DISPATCH_READY.
EXECUTED requires a fresh cloudAgentBcId (or provider-equivalent stable execution identity) and observed completion.

local-argv: Real child process exits 0 with expected stdout marker and cwd.
Real child process exits 42 with exact exit code and stdout/stderr captured.
Bounded sleep/hang produces TIMED_OUT rather than EXECUTED.
claude-code: AgentSwitchboard launches the real Claude Code CLI noninteractively.
Claude mutates a disposable fixture repository under an allowed REPO_EDIT policy.
An independent deterministic validator proves the expected filesystem/result state after Claude exits.
Missing binary/auth/timeout/structured-output failure paths fail closed.
Normalized receipt validates and records available native session/runtime identity.
cursor-cloud-agent: One AgentSwitchboard dispatch causes a real Cursor Task launch without a human bridge.
A fresh CloudAgent execution identity is captured.
Adapter observes completed/failed/timeout terminal state machine-readably.
A deterministic external artifact/result verifies the bounded task effect.
Wrong host, unavailable API/Task bridge, and timeout paths fail closed.

migration.legacyTriageDispatchReceipt: Keep tooling/harness/triage-consumer/dispatch/schemas/dispatch-receipt.schema.json as a compatibility surface until the generic runner can translate execution-receipt/v1 into the legacy lane receipt.
migration.cursorPr332Collision: PR #332 owns current Cursor dispatch implementation files. Shared contract work must not rewrite those files; Cursor adapter migration consumes/reconciles #332 after the contract floor lands.
migration.genericDispatcherTarget: dispatch_lanes.py becomes a consumer of the execution-adapter registry; harness-specific execution branches move behind adapters only after conformance proof.

proofCeiling: Contract shape, synthetic/public-safe fixtures, semantic invariants, and deterministic static validation only. This contract does not prove any adapter runtime, provider delivery, native session execution, Cursor Task completion, Claude Code execution, deployment, or operator acceptance.
